title: A fireball over Campo de Criptana: meteor, UFO or clay jar?
excerpt: A fireball shaped like a clay jar crossed the sky over Campo de Criptana in 1826. The locals took it for a prodigy. Meteor, UFO or collective hallucination?
content:
At 7:50 in the morning on February 14, 1826, the residents of Campo de Criptana saw an extraordinarily large ball of fire cross the sky, shaped like a large earthenware jar turned upside down and with a tail of smoke. The story comes from a Milenio 3 special (Cadena SER), which recalled it as one of the first UFO cases in Spain. At foro3d.com we wonder how those Manchegan peasants experienced a light fallen from the sky more than a century before anyone spoke of flying saucers.

What the witnesses said and what scholars say 🔭

The news was published by the Gaceta de Madrid on February 23 and later by the Diario Mercantil de Cádiz and the Diario Balear. According to those who saw it closest, it fell north of the town, toward the road to Quintanar, but no remains were found. Its light was so intense that many thought dawn had broken all at once. In contrast to the later UFO interpretation, scholars see in it a superbolide, an especially bright meteor. The difference between the two readings remains open.

The jar that never appeared 🏺

An earthenware jar turned upside down crossing the Manchegan sky sounds like a scene from a fairy tale, and yet no one found the vessel or a single fragment toward the road to Quintanar. Perhaps it disintegrated in the air, perhaps the countryside swallowed it. If you have any clue about that double dawn of February 14, tell us: meteor, UFO, or simply a jar of fire?
